head: 9007cee1
note: Pseudo-code written by the reviewing agent; explain_check.py verifies every step against the cited lines.

steps.text: a class `Foo` marked `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]`
it has a public property `Member` with no key attribute
the MessagePack analyzer runs on this code through `VerifyCS.Test`
exactly one diagnostic is expected: `MsgPack004` on the property name `Member`; any missing or extra diagnostic fails the test

does_not_check: It does not compare the diagnostic's message text; the markup only fixes the id and the location.
It does not check that the suppressed type still serializes at run time.
notes: Also passes on base (old-vs-new-tests.json), so it pins existing behaviour and is not evidence for the fix (C-2234-07).

steps.text: a class `Foo` marked `MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)`, which does not allow private members
it has a private field `member` with `[Key(0)]`
the MessagePack analyzer runs on this code through `VerifyCS.Test`
exactly one diagnostic is expected: `MsgPack015` on the `MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)` attribute; any missing or extra diagnostic fails the test

does_not_check: It does not compare the diagnostic's message text; the markup only fixes the id and the location.
It does not check the code fix that the diagnostic offers.
notes: Also passes on base (old-vs-new-tests.json), so it pins existing behaviour and is not evidence for the fix (C-2234-07).

steps.text: a plain class `Other` with no MessagePack attribute
a class `Foo` marked `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` with a `[Key(0)]` property `Member` of type `Other`
the MessagePack analyzer runs on this code through `VerifyCS.Test`
exactly one diagnostic is expected: `MsgPack003` on the property name `Member`; any missing or extra diagnostic fails the test

does_not_check: It does not compare the diagnostic's message text; the markup only fixes the id and the location.
It does not combine an unserializable member type with a duplicate or mixed key, the case where the branch drops this diagnostic (C-2234-04).
notes: Also passes on base (old-vs-new-tests.json), so it pins existing behaviour and is not evidence for the fix (C-2234-07).

steps.text: a class `Foo` marked `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]`
two properties `Member1` and `Member2` that both carry `[Key(0)]`
the MessagePack analyzer runs on this code through `VerifyCS.Test`
exactly one diagnostic is expected: `MsgPack005` covering the second member (its `[Key(0)]` and declaration); any extra diagnostic, such as an analyzer crash report, fails the test

does_not_check: It does not compare the diagnostic's message text; the markup only fixes the id and the location. So it does not show the message is 'must be unique'.
It does not cover a `[Key(null)]` member, where the analyzer still crashes on the branch (C-2234-03).
notes: Fails on base with 2 diagnostics instead of the expected 1 (the analyzer also threw) and passes on the branch.

steps.text: a class `Foo` marked `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]`
two properties `Member1` and `Member2` that both carry the same string key `[Key(""a"")]` (the doubled quotes are escaping inside the test's source string)
the MessagePack analyzer runs on this code through `VerifyCS.Test`
exactly one diagnostic is expected: `MsgPack005` covering the second member (its `[Key(""a"")]` and declaration); any extra diagnostic, such as an analyzer crash report, fails the test

does_not_check: It does not compare the diagnostic's message text; the markup only fixes the id and the location. So it does not show the message is 'must be unique'.
It does not check fields; only properties are used, although the fix was pasted into the fields loop too (C-2234-06).
notes: Fails on base with 2 diagnostics instead of the expected 1 (the analyzer also threw) and passes on the branch.

steps.text: a class `Foo` marked `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]`
two properties `Member1` and `Member2` that use different key kinds: `[Key(0)]` (a number) and `[Key(""Member2"")]` (a string)
the MessagePack analyzer runs on this code through `VerifyCS.Test`
exactly one diagnostic is expected: `MsgPack005` covering the second member (its `[Key(""Member2"")]` and declaration); any extra diagnostic, such as an analyzer crash report, fails the test

does_not_check: It does not compare the diagnostic's message text; the markup only fixes the id and the location. So it cannot tell 'must be of the same type' from 'must be unique'; both share this id.
It does not try a string key first and a number key second, nor a member whose type is also unserializable (C-2234-04).
notes: Fails on base with 2 diagnostics instead of the expected 1 (the analyzer also threw) and passes on the branch.

steps.text: a class `Foo` marked plain `[MessagePackObject]`, so source generation is NOT suppressed
two properties `Member1` and `Member2` that both carry `[Key(0)]`
the MessagePack analyzer runs on this code through `VerifyCS.Test`
exactly one diagnostic is expected: `MsgPack005` covering the second member (its `[Key(0)]` and declaration); any extra diagnostic, such as an analyzer crash report, fails the test

does_not_check: It does not compare the diagnostic's message text; the markup only fixes the id and the location.
It runs only the analyzer, not the source generator, so it does not check what the generator emits for this type.
notes: Fails on base with 2 diagnostics instead of the expected 1 (the analyzer also threw) and passes on the branch.

steps.text: (per the test's comment) `MsgPack011`, `MsgPack016` and `MsgPack017` only matter when a formatter is generated
a non-partial class `Foo` marked `[MessagePackObject(AllowPrivate = true, SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]`
it has a private field `member`, an init-only property `Prop1` with a default value, and a plain property `Prop2`, keyed `[Key(0)]`, `[Key(1)]`, `[Key(2)]`
the MessagePack analyzer runs on this code through `VerifyCS.Test` with no expected-diagnostic markup
`RunAsync()` passes only if no diagnostic at all is reported, because `TestCode = input` carries no expected-diagnostic markup; there is no explicit assert

does_not_check: It has no control case: it does not show these diagnostics would appear for the same type without `SuppressSourceGeneration`.
It does not say which member is meant to trigger which of the three skipped diagnostics.
notes: Also passes on base (old-vs-new-tests.json), so it pins existing behaviour and is not evidence for the fix (C-2234-07).

steps.text: a type `SuppressedSourceGenerationType` marked `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` with `Id` under `[Key(0)]` and `Name` under `[Key(1)]`
the test asks the source-generated resolver `GeneratedMessagePackResolver.Instance` for a formatter for that type
it asserts the answer is null (`Assert.Null`)

does_not_check: It does not look at the generated files; it only asks the resolver at run time.
It does not check that the analyzer still validates the type.
notes: Never ran here: the execution test project does not build on base or branch (CS9057, generator not loaded), so the result is unknown (C-2234-08).

steps.text: a type `SuppressedSourceGenerationType` marked `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` with `Id` under `[Key(0)]` and `Name` under `[Key(1)]`
a value with `Id = 7` and `Name = "seven"`
it is serialized to bytes and deserialized back, both with `MessagePackSerializerOptions.Standard`
it asserts `Assert.Equal(7, result.Id)` and `Assert.Equal("seven", result.Name)`

does_not_check: Despite its name, it does not check which resolver handled the type; it only uses the standard options.
It does not check the serialized bytes, only that the value survives a round trip.
notes: Never ran here: the execution test project does not build on base or branch (CS9057, generator not loaded), so the result is unknown (C-2234-08).
